Removes one or more marks by name, or every mark at once with --all — the marks 'kx state drop --all' deliberately leaves behind.

Names rather than row numbers: the mark listing carries no index column, because a mark is spent by the name it was given. A name that is not a mark refuses the whole call, so a typo partway through leaves every mark in place.

## Usage

```text
kx unmark [OPTIONS] [name...]
```

## Arguments

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `[name]...` | Mark names to remove |

## Options

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--all` | Remove every mark |

## Global options

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--no-color` | Disable styled output |
| `-h, --help` | Show this message and exit |

## Examples

```bash
kx unmark api
kx unmark api web db
kx unmark --all
```
